name: Rythu Bharosa (crop investment support)
what_you_get: Crop investment support of ₹12,000 per acre per year, credited to the farmer's bank account by DBT. The state releases it season by season (for example, the Vanakalam/kharif 2026 release in June–July 2026).
who_can_apply: Pattadars (land-owning farmers) for cultivable land recorded on the Bhu Bharati (Dharani) portal
RoFR (forest rights) patta holders
Non-cultivable land is excluded
how_to_apply: No separate application form is described in the GO: assistance is paid by DBT based on land records in Bhu Bharati
Make sure your land record and bank account details are correct
For problems, contact your Agriculture Extension Officer (AEO) or Mandal Agriculture Officer (MAO); contact lists are on rythubharosa.telangana.gov.in
source_title: G.O.Rt.No.18, Agriculture & Cooperation (Agri-II) Dept, Govt of Telangana, dated 10-01-2025 – Rythu Bharosa Scheme 2025 guidelines
verification_note: GO (Telugu, scanned) says scheme runs from 26 Jan 2025 at ₹12,000/acre/year, for cultivable land on Bhu Bharati, incl. RoFR pattadars, via DBT. Telangana govt press releases of 30 Jun 2026 and 10 Jul 2026 confirm ₹9,000 crore credited to 73.30 lakh farmers in the 2026 round. Replaces Rythu Bandhu. Per-season split not stated in the GO.

name: Annadatha Sukhibhava – PM-KISAN
what_you_get: ₹20,000 per year per eligible farmer family, which includes the ₹6,000 paid by the Government of India under PM-KISAN. It is paid in instalments (e.g. ₹7,000 per farmer as the first instalment for Kharif 2026, released 20 June 2026).
who_can_apply: Landholder farmer families who collectively own cultivable land in Andhra Pradesh
Landless cultivators (the state budget says they will also get ₹20,000 per year from state funds)
how_to_apply: No separate application process is described in the budget document
Check your eligibility and payment status with Aadhaar on annadathasukhibhava.ap.gov.in ("Know Your Status")
For problems, contact your village agriculture staff / local agriculture office
source_title: Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27, Volume VII/2 (Scheduled Tribes Component) – Agriculture Department, 1.1 Annadatha Sukhibhava Scheme
verification_note: Official AP budget 2026-27 states ₹20,000/yr incl. ₹6,000 PM-KISAN; launched 02.08.2025. Budget speech: 2025-26 paid ₹6,660 crore to 46.86 lakh families. AIR (20 Jun 2026) reports ₹7,000/farmer Kharif 2026 instalment. Replaced YSR Rythu Bharosa. Landless-cultivator payment is stated as a commitment; actual payout not confirmed.

name: Crop insurance – PMFBY / RWBCIS (voluntary enrolment)
what_you_get: Insurance against crop loss from natural calamities, pests and diseases in Kharif and Rabi. Since Rabi 2024-25 enrolment is voluntary and the farmer pays a small premium; the State and Centre pay the rest of the premium equally.
who_can_apply: Farmers in Andhra Pradesh growing notified crops (enrolment is voluntary)
how_to_apply: Enrol through your bank or a Common Service Centre (CSC) before the season's cut-off date
Pay the farmer's share of the premium at enrolment
source_title: Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27, Volume VII/2 – Agriculture Department, 1.2 Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
verification_note: Official AP budget confirms PMFBY and RWBCIS implemented with voluntary enrolment from Rabi 2024-25, farmer pays nominal premium. Premium rates and cut-off dates not given in this source. This replaced AP's earlier free (state-paid) crop insurance.

name: Zero-interest agricultural loans through co-operatives
what_you_get: Agricultural loans at zero percent interest through co-operative credit institutions. For 2026-27 the state targets ₹30,000 crore of such loans to 38 lakh farmers.
who_can_apply: Farmers in Karnataka who borrow from co-operative credit societies/banks (e.g. PACS)
how_to_apply: Apply for a crop loan at your Primary Agricultural Co-operative Society (PACS) or co-operative bank
Ask the society for the current loan limit and repayment terms
verification_note: Official budget speech confirms zero-interest agricultural loans target for 2026-27, and ₹22,000 crore disbursed to 25 lakh farmers in 2025-26 (as of Feb 2026). Per-farmer loan limit is not stated in this source.

name: Krishi Bhagya (farm ponds)
what_you_get: Government support to build farm ponds so rain-fed farmers can store water for protective irrigation. 12,000 more farm ponds were planned for 2025-26.
who_can_apply: Farmers in Karnataka, especially in rain-fed/dry areas (exact eligibility not stated in the budget source)
how_to_apply: Contact your nearest Raitha Samparka Kendra or taluk Assistant Director of Agriculture
verification_note: Budget 2025-26 confirms 12,000 more ponds in 2025-26; Budget 2026-27 reports 32,138 farm ponds built at ₹363 crore. Subsidy rate per pond is not stated in these sources. Helpline is the department's Raitha Call Center listed on raitamitra.karnataka.gov.in.

name: Karnataka Raitha Suraksha – Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (crop insurance)
hindi_name: ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ರೈತ ಸುರಕ್ಷಾ ಪ್ರಧಾನ ಮಂತ್ರಿ ಫಸಲ್ ಭೀಮಾ ಯೋಜನೆ (Kannada)
what_you_get: Crop insurance against crop loss under PMFBY, run in Karnataka through the Samrakshane portal. The state reports crop insurance claims of ₹6,213 crore settled for 51 lakh farmers.
who_can_apply: Farmers in Karnataka growing notified crops in notified areas
how_to_apply: Enrol for the season on the Samrakshane portal (samrakshane.karnataka.gov.in) or through your bank before the cut-off date
Check application/claim status on the same portal
as_of: Budget 2026-27; Samrakshane portal showed 'Enrolment for Khariff 2026 is OPEN' (checked 2026-10-21)
verification_note: Budget speech confirms claims settled; Samrakshane portal lists 2025-26 and 2026-27 seasons. Premium rates and cut-off dates not given in these sources. Claims figure is cumulative over the government's term, not one year.

name: Kuruvai Special Package 2026 (delta and non-delta districts)
what_you_get: Input support for Kuruvai/Kar/Sornavari paddy (total ₹134.83 crore): ₹4,000 per acre back-end subsidy for machine transplanting or direct-seeded rice; paddy micronutrient mixture at 50% subsidy or ₹147.6/acre; liquid bio-fertiliser at 50% or ₹60/acre; seed paddy at 50% or ₹10/kg (older varieties) / ₹20/kg (newer varieties), whichever is less.
who_can_apply: Delta package: all farmers of Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Cuddalore, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai, Trichy and Ariyalur districts
Non-delta package: paddy farmers in other districts in the Kar/Kuruvai/Sornavari season
how_to_apply: Contact your block Agriculture office / Assistant Director of Agriculture
Check components on the TN Agriculture Department 'Schemes 2026-27' page (tnagrisnet.tn.gov.in) and register through the department
source_title: TN Agriculture–Farmers Welfare Dept, Schemes 2026-27: Kuruvai Special Package scheme for Delta Districts 2026-27 (tnagrisnet)
verification_note: Announced by CM C. Joseph Vijay (TVK govt) in DIPR press release 218 of 12.06.2026: ₹77.50 cr delta + ₹57.33 cr non-delta. Rates and documents from the department's 2026-27 scheme data. Seasonal (June–Sept); news (PMK, Aug 2026) reported delays in benefits reaching farmers.

name: Chief Minister's Mannuyir Kaathu Mannuyir Kaappom Scheme 2026-27 (soil health)
hindi_name: முதலமைச்சரின் மண்ணுயிர் காத்து மன்னுயிர் காப்போம் திட்டம் (Tamil)
what_you_get: Subsidised green manure seeds to improve soil health: Rs.70 per kg or 50% of the actual cost, whichever is lower.
who_can_apply: Farmers of all districts except Chennai, the Nilgiris, Coimbatore and Kanyakumari
how_to_apply: Contact your block Agriculture office / Agriculture Extension Centre
Details on the TN Agriculture Department 'Schemes 2026-27' page (tnagrisnet.tn.gov.in)
source_title: TN Agriculture–Farmers Welfare Dept, Schemes 2026-27: Chief Minister's Mannuyir Kaathu Mannuyir Kaappom Scheme 2026-27 (tnagrisnet)
verification_note: DMK-era scheme still listed under 2026-27 by the TVK government's Agriculture Department; only the green-manure component is listed there now. TVK revised agri budget (6 Aug 2026, AIR) also announced a Soil Fertility Mission (₹122 crore) – details not verified.

name: Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana (NSMNY)
what_you_get: Rs. 6,000 a year from the Maharashtra government, paid in three equal instalments of Rs. 2,000 by DBT to an Aadhaar-linked bank account. This is on top of PM-KISAN, so an eligible farmer family gets Rs. 12,000 a year from both schemes.
who_can_apply: Farmer families in Maharashtra that are eligible for and receiving PM-KISAN (myScheme: cultivable land holding as on 01.02.2019)

Same exclusions as PM-KISAN apply (e.g. income-tax payers, serving/retired government employees, pensioners with Rs. 10,000+/month pension, constitutional post holders, registered professionals, NRIs)
how_to_apply: No separate NSMNY registration: register on the PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in); eligible PM-KISAN beneficiaries automatically get NSMNY
Keep the bank account Aadhaar-linked and DBT-enabled
Check beneficiary status on nsmny.mahait.org
source_title: myScheme: Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana (Commissionerate of Agriculture, Maharashtra)
as_of: GR dated 03 Sep 2025 (7th instalment, Apr-Jul 2025); checked 2026-10-21
verification_note: myScheme (content read via its public API; page is JS-rendered) gives Rs. 6,000/yr in 3 instalments on top of PM-KISAN. Official NSMNY portal hosts GRs for instalments 1-7; the 7th-instalment GR (03 Sep 2025) released Rs. 1932.72 crore for Apr-Jul 2025, confirming it ran in 2025-26. Later instalments not checked. Helpline and email are from the NSMNY portal Contact Us.

name: Mukhyamantri (Chief Minister) Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana
what_you_get: Extra Rs. 3,000 a year from the Rajasthan government (raised from Rs. 2,000 in Budget 2025-26), paid by DBT at Rs. 1,000 per instalment. This is on top of PM-KISAN's Rs. 6,000.
who_can_apply: Farmers in Rajasthan who are beneficiaries of PM-KISAN
how_to_apply: No separate application is described in the official source; the top-up goes by DBT to farmers benefiting under PM-KISAN
Check status via 'Mukhyamantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana Status' on the Jan Soochna Portal (jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in)
source_title: Government of Rajasthan, Economic Review 2025-26 (Finance Department, Budget 2026-27 documents)
as_of: Economic Review 2025-26 (data up to Dec 2025); checked 2026-10-21
verification_note: Official Economic Review 2025-26 states the annual top-up was raised from Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 3,000 in Budget 2025-26, paid at Rs. 1,000 per farmer; 4th instalment Rs. 717.96 crore to 71.79 lakh farmers. Eligibility (PM-KISAN beneficiaries) is from the Economic Review 2024-25 (finance.rajasthan.gov.in/docs/budget/statebudget/2025-2026/EconomicReviewE.pdf). DD News (16 Aug 2026) reports another Rs. 1,000-per-farmer instalment to ~67 lakh farmers, so it is still running. Note: some news counts Rs. 9,000 as Centre+State combined.

name: Small and Marginal Older Farmers' Samman Pension Scheme (Laghu evam Seemant Vriddhajan Krishak Samman Pension Yojana)
hindi_name: लघु एवं सीमांत वृद्धजन कृषक सम्मान पेंशन योजना
what_you_get: A monthly pension of Rs. 1,250 for older small and marginal farmers. This is a state pension, not a PM-KISAN top-up.
who_can_apply: Small and marginal farmers resident in Rajasthan
Women aged 55 years or more; men aged 58 years or more
how_to_apply: Apply online through Rajasthan SSO (sso.rajasthan.gov.in) using Jan Aadhaar, as described on myScheme (Social Justice and Empowerment Department scheme)
Pension stops if the farmer leaves the small/marginal category or migrates out of Rajasthan
source_title: Government of Rajasthan, Economic Review 2025-26 (Finance Department, Budget 2026-27 documents)
verification_note: Economic Review 2025-26 gives Rs. 1,250/month, 1.97 lakh beneficiaries, Rs. 234.89 crore spent up to Dec 2025 (2024-25 Review gave Rs. 1,150). Text is from a two-column infographic, read carefully. myScheme page (myscheme.gov.in/schemes/slesvkspy) still shows older amounts (Rs. 750/1,000) - do not use those; application steps taken from myScheme.

name: Mukhyamantri Kisan Kalyan Yojana
what_you_get: Rs. 6,000 a year from the Madhya Pradesh government, in addition to PM-KISAN (so Rs. 12,000 a year together). In July 2026 two instalments were paid together, Rs. 4,000 per farmer.
who_can_apply: Farmers of Madhya Pradesh who are beneficiaries of the scheme (it runs alongside PM-KISAN)
Farmers who burn crop stubble (narwai) are denied the benefit (state decision effective 1 May 2025)
how_to_apply: Official releases do not describe a separate current application; payment is made directly to beneficiary bank accounts
Check beneficiary status under 'CM Kisan Kalyan Yojna Beneficiary Status' on the SAARA portal (saara.mp.gov.in)
source_title: MP Jansampark (mpinfo.org) release, 12 Aug 2025: CM to transfer 2025-26 second instalment of Mukhyamantri Kisan Kalyan Yojana
verification_note: Official MP Public Relations Dept release (12 Aug 2025) states Rs. 6,000/yr in addition to PM-KISAN. Release of 27 Jul 2026 (https://www.mpinfo.org/Home/TodaysNews?newsid=%C2%B2%C2%B0%C2%B2%C2%B6%C2%B0%C2%B7%C2%B2%C2%B7%C3%8E%C2%B1%C2%B6%C2%B3&fontname=Mangal&LocID=32&pubdate=07%2F27%2F2026) confirms Rs. 3,308 crore to 82.70 lakh+ farmers, Rs. 4,000 each in one go. Release of 24 Apr 2025 (https://www.mpinfo.org/Home/TodaysNews?newsid=%C2%B2%C2%B0%C2%B2%C2%B5%C2%B0%C2%B4%C2%B2%C2%B4%C3%8E%C2%B4%C2%B2%C2%B9&fontname=Mangal&LocID=32&pubdate=04%2F24%2F2025) says stubble burners lose the benefit from 1 May 2025. mpinfo pages load text by script; content read via the site's own news API. Older 2020 releases show Rs. 4,000/yr - outdated.

name: COP-34 Financial Assistance to Farmers for Interest Subvention (Kisan Credit Card crop-loan interest help)
hindi_name: COP-34 વ્યાજ સહાય માટે ખેડૂતોને નાણાકીય સહાય
what_you_get: The Gujarat government pays 4% interest subvention on short-term crop loans up to Rs. 3,00,000 when the farmer repays on time (once in a financial year).
who_can_apply: Farmers in Gujarat who took a short-term Kharif crop loan (1 April - 30 September) from a Primary Agricultural Credit Cooperative Society, District Central Cooperative Bank, nationalised, Gramin or private bank
The loan must be repaid on time
how_to_apply: No individual application: the lending bank submits the combined interest-subvention proposal to the Registrar, Co-operative Societies, Gujarat, Gandhinagar
Repay the crop loan on time to qualify
source_title: myScheme: COP-34 Financial Assistance to Farmer for Interest Subvention (Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Dept, Gujarat)
verification_note: Amount and process from myScheme (read via its API). Running in 2026-27: the department's official Budget Book 2026-27 (agri.gujarat.gov.in/Home/main/BudgetBook202627) has head 2425-00-107-18 'COP-34 Financial assistance to farmer for subvention of interest' with Rs. 1,450 crore budgeted. Myscheme describes it for Kharif-season loans only.

name: Assistance in Cow Maintenance Expenses to Farmers Practicing Completely Natural Farming Based on Indigenous Cows (AGR-8)
what_you_get: Rs. 900 per month (Rs. 10,800 a year) to maintain one indigenous (desi) cow, for farmers doing fully natural farming. The benefit is given only once.
who_can_apply: Farmers in Gujarat practising natural farming on at least 1 acre (40 guntha)
Must own a native/indigenous cow with an identification tag
One beneficiary per land account (8-A)
how_to_apply: Apply online on the i-Khedut portal (ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in) under the scheme when applications are open
Print the application and submit it with listed documents to the Gram Sevak / BTM / ATM / Project Director-ATMA
Track status in the i-Khedut Applicant Corner
source_title: myScheme: Scheme to Provide Assistance in Cow Maintenance Expenses to Farmers Practicing Completely Natural Farming Based on Indigenous Cows (Gujarat)
verification_note: Amount, eligibility and steps from myScheme (read via its API). Running in 2026-27: official AFW&CD Budget Book 2026-27 head 2401-00-109-09 'AGR-8 A Scheme to provide assistance to farmers family for natural farming to maintain indigenous cow (100% state)' with Rs. 150 crore budgeted. Application windows on i-Khedut open for limited periods.

name: Crop Residue Management (CRM) Machinery Subsidy Scheme
what_you_get: 50% of the machine cost for individual farmers buying crop residue management machines (e.g. Super SMS, Happy Seeder, Super Seeder), and 80% (projects up to Rs. 30 lakh) for cooperative societies, FPOs, panchayats and rural entrepreneurs setting up Custom Hiring Centres.
who_can_apply: Individual farmers in Punjab (50%)
Cooperative societies of farmers, registered farmer societies, FPOs, panchayats and rural entrepreneurs setting up Custom Hiring Centres (80%)
how_to_apply: Apply under 'CRM Machinery Scheme' on the Punjab Agriculture Department subsidy portal agrimachinerypb.com when the state opens applications
Buy only from approved manufacturers/vendors and approved machine list shown on the portal
source_title: PIB, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare: Stubble Burning (18 Mar 2025)
verification_note: Centrally funded scheme (since 2018-19) implemented by Punjab Agriculture Dept; rates from PIB 18 Mar 2025. Portal agrimachinerypb.com (Dept of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Punjab) shows 'Apply Under CRM Machinery Scheme'. All India Radio (Feb 2026) reports Rs. 395 crore disbursed in Kharif 2025 with 50-80% subsidies. Application windows are seasonal; exact 2026 window not verified.
